No panel dissent is attached, so no dissent answers are owed; the judgment nonetheless changed, and a complete assessment is returned.

WHAT MOVED. Since the incumbent was adopted the ledger has taken on a substantial new tranche of records, and two per-claim verdicts change on them.

(1) ORCH-C031 goes well_supported → established. The Gran Sasso null is no longer a single experiment: ORCH-E047 and ORCH-E049 record an independent underground germanium collaboration finding no 1/E collapse radiation in 37.5 kg-y of enriched exposure and stating, in its own words, that this adds significance to the exclusion of the parameter-free Diósi–Penrose model. Two independent nulls in the same channel, one of them co-authored by the model's co-originator, put the exclusion beyond reasonable dispute.

(2) ORCH-C021 goes provisionally_supported → mixed. The direction of the polymerization effect now has partial cross-lab support (ORCH-E056), but the same dataset shows the effect size spanning +6.1% to +46.8% depending purely on how scattering is treated (ORCH-E075) and, at 295 nm — the wavelength most selective for tryptophan, and therefore the one where comparison with a tryptophan-only excitonic model is most meaningful — the sign reverses between absorbance treatments (ORCH-E076 through ORCH-E079). An observable whose sign is not fixed at the diagnostic wavelength cannot be graded as provisionally supporting the model that predicted its direction. ORCH-C063 records, from the modellers themselves, that structural variability suppresses the maximal superradiant enhancement the collective reading needs.

(3) Verdicts I considered moving and held. ORCH-C026 stays mixed. The exchange is now complete — ORCH-E087 through ORCH-E090 are the authors' quantitative reply, showing the classical intermolecular zero-quantum-coherence bound at their sequence parameters is 0.4% of initial magnetization, 0.13% with relaxation, and conceding "we have not measured iZQC". That answers the specific mechanism Warren proposed, which is why the reasoning changes. It is not independent adjudication, the authors concede their classical bound rests on models derived for chemical solutions, and no laboratory has replicated the protocol; so the verdict holds. ORCH-C030 stays unresolved, but the escape recorded at ORCH-E019 is now much more expensive: ORCH-E046 bounds the Diósi–Penrose regularization length above any nuclear size through mechanical acceleration noise, a channel no "Penrose predicts no radiation" argument reaches, and ORCH-E051 records a semiclassical construction that reproduces Penrose's rate exactly and fixes its prefactor at 1/2 — so "the tested model was never Penrose's" becomes a question about which dynamics, not about whether any dynamics lands on the relation. ORCH-E071 and ORCH-E052, from the co-originator, are why it is still unresolved rather than contradicted: the rate carries an unspecified constant, and the dynamics that would make it testable is precisely what the two originators do not agree on.

(4) The incumbent assessment was also structurally incomplete for a reader: a null steelman, no per-claim treatments, no components, no research priority. Those are supplied here.

SELECTION. The featured set goes from 19 to 24, adding the competing accounts and cruxes the catalog now carries. ORCH-C044 is the serious quantum-but-not-microtubular rival: spin-dependent radical-pair chemistry modulating microtubule assembly, which offers a mechanism for the one result that most embarrasses the stability story (a stabilizer and a destabilizer shifting sensitivity the same way) and carries field- and isotope-dependent predictions of its own. ORCH-C057 is featured because it is the proponents' strongest load-bearing assertion — that no rival target has a published model reproducing Meyer–Overton — and it is featured with credibility unresolved and diagnosticity high, which is the honest shape: nobody has done the survey that would settle it either way. ORCH-C063 is featured because it is the crux on which the collective-optics reading turns. ORCH-C046 and ORCH-C047 are featured because they are the two new independent constraints on the physics conjunct, one of them through a channel the under-specification escape does not reach. The fine-grained collapse-rate claims (ORCH-C065 through ORCH-C069) stay catalogued under ORCH-C030 and are cited in the prose where they bear.

CRUX ORDER. Fifteen items now exist. ORCH-R001 still leads: the coherence witness is the only measurement that could settle the biological half either way. ORCH-R014 is promoted to second because it is a desk item that would make ORCH-R001 scorable — publish the 310 K dephasing prediction and the pass/fail threshold before the spectroscopy, which the corpus audit (ORCH-E035) found the literature has never done. ORCH-R013 is placed high among the desk items because it prices the physics escape precisely.

PROSE. The article keeps the founding telling's spine and its best move — separating five propositions that the public argument slides between — and adds what the ledger now holds: a second underground null and a mechanical-channel bound; the co-originator's own statement that the rate carries an unspecified constant and that he and Penrose disagree about the dynamics; the metrology problem inside the flagship optical observable; the completed MRI exchange; the spin-chemistry rival; and an explicit side-by-side of the six live accounts, which the incumbent left implicit. Both plates are retained in place.

article:
For most of thirty years, Orch OR has been the theory you invoke to end a conversation. Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff propose that [each conscious moment is a gravitationally induced collapse of a quantum state orchestrated across tubulin proteins inside neuronal microtubules]{claim=ORCH-C001}, and the field's reply is a calculation: the brain is warm, wet and electrically noisy, quantum coherence there should last something like 10⁻¹³ seconds, and a neuron takes ten orders of magnitude longer to do anything. Case closed, and closed by a physicist rather than a partisan.

The biological half is no longer purely speculative. Microtubules move electronic excitation further than standard transfer theory predicts. Anesthetics measurably shorten that transport. A microtubule-stabilizing drug delays anesthetic unconsciousness in rats, then in mice. None of those results measures a coherence time, an entangled state, or a collapse event. Meanwhile experiments under an Italian mountain and in a South Dakota mine have killed the most natural version of Penrose's physics twice over, an independent laboratory finds the anesthesia effect running backwards, and AI systems are solving the kind of mathematics that motivated the whole idea in the first place.

The interesting thing about this case is how cleanly its rungs come apart — and how consistently the public argument, in both directions, refuses to let them.

## Five different propositions

Almost every confused exchange about Orch OR consists of silently sliding between these: quantum effects in microtubules, quantum coherence in microtubules, entanglement in microtubules, quantum computation in neurons, and Penrose gravitational collapse. The first is trivially true — all chemistry is quantum mechanics. The last is an unconfirmed proposal in the foundations of physics. They are not the same claim, and evidence for one is not evidence for the next.

So the ladder below this article separates them, and the separation produces verdicts that look strange until you see why. [Microtubules have collective electronic dynamics that a model of them as passive scaffolding does not predict]{claim=ORCH-C013} is assessed as well supported. [Neuronal microtubules sustain coherent states long enough and wide enough to support the computation the theory requires]{claim=ORCH-C010} is assessed as unresolved — not contradicted, *unmeasured*. And the headline thesis, which needs both, sits above them as unresolved on the strength of the weakest rung it depends on.

## What the microtubules actually do

{plate:IMG-ORCHOR-P01}

The pivotal experiment comes out of Gregory Scholes's ultrafast spectroscopy laboratory at Princeton. Shine ultraviolet light on polymerized microtubules, watch how tryptophan fluorescence lifetimes change as a quencher is added, and infer how far electronic excitation travels before it dissipates. The answer: [about 6.6 nanometres, which the authors report is not sufficiently explained by accepted Förster resonance energy transfer models even after accounting for tryptophan–tyrosine interactions]{claim=ORCH-C020}. Their own summary is that microtubules are, unexpectedly, effective light harvesters. Polymerization state matters; protofilament architecture does not — the kind of structure-dependence that argues against an artifact.

A partly independent group at Howard University reports that [organized tryptophan networks in microtubules form collective superradiant states, with fluorescence quantum yield rising with hierarchical organization as their model predicts]{claim=ORCH-C021}, and a 2026 cross-laboratory measurement in porcine tubulin reproduces the direction of that quantum-yield increase at 280 nanometre excitation. Microtubules are not inert beams. That is a real result and it would be worth knowing regardless of anyone's views about consciousness.

Now the part that proponent summaries skip. 6.6 nanometres is roughly the length of a single tubulin dimer, and the physics is femtoseconds to picoseconds. Orch OR needs milliseconds, across many tubulins, ideally across many neurons. That is a shortfall of many orders of magnitude in both time and space, and none of it has been closed. The superradiance work's arresting figure — collective states with radiative lifetimes of "tens of seconds" — measures how weakly a state couples to the light field, not how long it survives environmental dephasing. A state can be radiatively dark for seconds and decohere in femtoseconds. The most recent modelling of the same tryptophan geometry says so explicitly in its own methods: its lifetimes are defined within a Markovian radiative-loss model, with no solvent, ionic or vibrational bath anywhere in the calculation. Its authors add a disclaimer that proponent summaries tend to lose — that their results do not imply microtubules must use quantum correlations for neural processing at all.

The two numbers that would settle this rung do not exist. What exists instead is two calculations. Max Tegmark's paper puts microtubule decoherence at [10⁻¹³ to 10⁻²⁰ seconds against neural dynamical timescales of 10⁻³ to 10⁻¹]{claim=ORCH-C010}; Hagan, Hameroff and Tuszyński reply in the same journal that Tegmark modelled the wrong state — a soliton in superposition along the microtubule rather than the superposed protein conformations the theory proposes — and that correcting the assumptions yields 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴ seconds. Both are right that the other is arguing about a model. Neither measured a living microtubule. And even the proponents' own revised figure falls two to three orders of magnitude short of the roughly 25-millisecond conscious moment their theory names.

There is also a distinctive result from Anirban Bandyopadhyay's group at NIMS in Japan: [self-similar "triplet of triplet" resonance patterns in tubulin, in microtubules, and in a neuron's axon initial segment]{claim=ORCH-C022}, offered as the scale-bridging mechanism the theory requires to get from molecules to brains. Electromagnetic resonance is a classical observable, so even if the pattern is real it is not a coherence witness — and it has stood unreplicated for over a decade. The case editor's own primer, otherwise sympathetic, calls independent replication of this work "the missing piece," and draws the comparison that matters: the photosynthetic coherence results of 2007 were replicated many times over and founded a field.

### The measurement problem inside the measurement

One more thing has to be said about the optical observable, because it bears on every experiment anyone proposes to run against it. Microtubules scatter ultraviolet light strongly, and how you subtract that scattering from their absorbance changes the answer. In the 2026 cross-laboratory dataset, the polymerization-induced quantum-yield increase at 280 nanometres ranges from about +6% to about +47% depending purely on which of two defensible absorbance treatments is used. At 295 nanometres — the wavelength that excites tryptophan most selectively, and therefore the one where comparison with a tryptophan-only excitonic model is most meaningful — the two treatments do not merely differ in size. They *reverse sign*: about −59% on one branch, about +13% on the other. The authors decline to assign a single effect size there, and they are right to.

On top of which, the modellers report that [including realistic structural variability sharply reduces the maximal superradiant enhancement relative to an idealized ordered lattice]{claim=ORCH-C063}, even though a modest quantum yield survives. Two things come apart there, and only one of them is what the scale-bridging argument needs: a small yield trend that tolerates disorder, and a large cooperative radiative gain that does not.

This is a fixable, unglamorous problem — cuvette versus integrating-sphere geometry, independent turbidity measurement, measured polymer fraction — and it should be fixed before anyone spends a grant correlating this observable against anesthetic potency. Otherwise the experiment measures the correction rather than the physics.

## The anesthesia experiments, in both directions

This is the tractable part of the case, and the part with an actual empirical fight in it.

{plate:IMG-ORCHOR-P02}

The proponent line runs like this. Anesthetics reduce microtubule exciton diffusion in the Princeton experiment. An anesthesia laboratory at Penn with no Orch OR commitment [identified β-tubulin as the photolabelled target of an anthracene anesthetic and found microtubule stabilizers raising the concentration needed to immobilize tadpoles]{claim=ORCH-C011}. And then the behavioural result: a group at Wellesley gives rats a low dose of the microtubule stabilizer epothilone B and finds they [take 69 seconds longer to lose the righting reflex under isoflurane, a large standardized effect, blinded, with a control for anesthesia tolerance]{claim=ORCH-C023}. They reproduce the direction in mice, at 29 seconds and a smaller effect size, and say in their own abstract that it is not large against the variability between animals.

Then there is the result a fair map cannot omit. A group at Massachusetts General Hospital, independent of the Wellesley programme, runs the fuller version of the experiment — randomized, blinded, four drugs, full concentration–response curves rather than latency at one concentration — and finds [chronic epothilone D making mice markedly *more* sensitive to isoflurane, not less]{claim=ORCH-C024}. Worse for the simple story: the destabilizer vinblastine moves sensitivity the same direction as the stabilizer. No account based on microtubule stability predicts that. It suggests the operative variable might be general cellular disruption.

This does not refute the acute epothilone-B finding — different compound, different regimen, a single injection against two weeks of dosing. It does refute the generalization that stabilizing microtubules protects consciousness from anesthetics, which is how [the claim that microtubule manipulation changes anesthetic susceptibility]{claim=ORCH-C012} is usually presented in public. Credit where it is due: the Wellesley group cites the contradictory study in its own abstract rather than omitting it.

And the sharpest objection to the whole anesthesia arm comes from inside its flagship experiment. The Princeton paper also tests picrotoxin — a convulsant, pharmacologically the opposite of an anesthetic — and finds it affecting the same assay comparably. If a convulsant and two anesthetics all suppress the signal, the assay is measuring how perturbable microtubule photophysics is by small hydrophobic molecules, not anything specific to anesthesia. The experiment that would resolve this is not exotic: a potency series across eight or more agents with nonimmobilizers and matched non-anesthetic controls, free aqueous concentration measured, and the predicted correlation registered in advance. It has not been run.

## A quantum rival with no microtubules in it

One genuinely strange data point sits off to the side. [Xenon isotopes bearing nuclear spin are markedly weaker anesthetics than spin-zero isotopes, at identical calculated polarizability]{claim=ORCH-C025} — published in *Anesthesiology*, randomized across 80 mice. Nuclear spin is a quantum property with no classical polarizability explanation available. It is hard to fit into a pharmacology with no quantum degrees of freedom in it.

It is also thinner than its citation record implies. This case's own re-analysis of the four published arms finds that the headline xenon-alone potencies are calculated by the authors from co-administration with isoflurane rather than directly measured; that the published dispersions are of unstated type, so a reader cannot tell from the accessible record whether the arms overlap; and that in eight years the result has never been replicated, extended with further isotope arms, or preceded by any isotope-resolved measurement. What the numbers do support, descriptively, is the *shape* of the pattern: two mass units change potency by a few per cent within each spin pair, while one mass unit across the spin boundary changes it by thirty. A smooth mass confound — diffusion, solubility — does not make a step like that.

But notice where the step points. Nuclear spin implicates *some* spin-sensitive molecular process and says nothing about where. The published rival is explicit: a radical-pair model with hyperfine coupling to the xenon nucleus, sited at a receptor rather than in the cytoskeleton. The same group extends the idea to the cytoskeleton itself, proposing that [spin dynamics of a naturally occurring tryptophan-cation/superoxide radical pair modulate microtubule polymerization, so that microtubule density depends on ambient magnetic field strength]{claim=ORCH-C044}. That is a model fit with free parameters, not a measurement — but it is the only account on the table that offers a mechanism for chemically opposite microtubule drugs moving anesthetic sensitivity the same way, and it makes field- and isotope-dependent predictions that a modest experiment could test. Quantum biology in anesthesia and Orch OR are not the same hypothesis, and this is where they come apart most cleanly.

## The physics half, tested under two mountains

Penrose's contribution is separable from all of the biology and testable without any of it. He proposes that [superpositions of sufficiently different mass distributions collapse objectively, with a lifetime set by the gravitational self-energy of the difference]{claim=ORCH-C030} — τ ≈ ℏ/E_G. This is a proposal in quantum foundations that mainstream physicists have their own reasons to test.

They have tested a version of it, twice. If gravity collapses wavefunctions in the standard stochastic way, charged particles should faintly radiate. A team including Lajos Diósi — co-originator of the model under test — looked with an ultra-low-background germanium detector at the [Gran Sasso underground laboratory](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-020-1008-4) and [found nothing, tightening the bound on the model's spatial cutoff by three orders of magnitude and ruling out, in their own words, "the natural parameter-free version of the Diósi–Penrose model"]{claim=ORCH-C031}. Then an independent collaboration, [the Majorana Demonstrator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01343), went looking for the same 1/E X-ray signature in 37.5 kilogram-years of enriched germanium and [found no evidence of it between 19 and 100 keV]{claim=ORCH-C047}, improving the bound again and, in its own closing words, adding significance to the exclusion of the parameter-free model. Methodologically these are the best experiments anywhere in this case, and both came out negative.

The published escape from them is real: a philosopher of physics, Kelvin McQueen, pressed the point that Penrose's criterion is a characteristic-lifetime relation, not a stochastic master equation, and so makes no radiation prediction. That is correct, and it is why this rung is assessed as unresolved rather than refuted. But the escape has become expensive, for three reasons the ledger now holds.

First, there is a second channel. [LISA Pathfinder's measured relative acceleration noise between two free-falling test masses bounds the Diósi–Penrose regularization length above 40 femtometres — larger than the size of any nucleus]{claim=ORCH-C046}. That is mechanical momentum diffusion, not photon emission, so "no radiation is predicted" does not reach it. Escaping both channels now requires a collapse that injects neither energy nor momentum into matter.

Second, at least one dynamics does land on Penrose's relation exactly. Diósi reports that [the semiclassical least-decoherence construction he developed with Tilloy reproduces the conjectured rate and makes its numeric constant unique]{claim=ORCH-C066}, with prefactor one half. So "the tested model was never Penrose's" is now a claim about *which* dynamics, not about whether any dynamics reaches the relation — and whether that particular dynamics is already excluded by the bounded channels is a question a careful desk calculation could answer.

Third, the co-originator is franker about the state of the proposal than either side's advocates. He writes that the rate is specified only up to an unspecified numeric constant, that its apparent freedom from parameters may be illusory because the expression diverges for point-like masses and so needs exactly the short-length regulator experiments are bounding, and — closing the article — that [he and Penrose agree the superposition should collapse after a time of order ℏ/E_Δ and disagree on how it happens, "smoothly, suddenly, or some other way"]{claim=ORCH-C069}.

That is the honest position: the lifetime relation is untested, every dynamics so far proposed to realize it is being squeezed, and the thing that would make it decisively testable is the thing its two originators do not agree on.

## The living-brain signal, and its finished exchange

One experiment claims to see non-classical behaviour directly. [Zero-quantum-coherence MRI of living human brains produces heartbeat-timed signals that depend on conscious awareness, which the experimenters interpret as witnessing entanglement]{claim=ORCH-C026}; subjects report the signal disappearing as they fall asleep. Warren S. Warren, a leading NMR methodologist, replied in the same journal that the data provide no evidence to justify the claim and show only that living tissue is complex, multicompartmental and imprecisely characterized by MRI.

The authors' reply is now on the record, and it is quantitative rather than rhetorical. For their own sequence parameters they compute that the classical intermolecular zero-quantum-coherence signal could reach at most 0.4% of the initial magnetization, falling to 0.13% once relaxation is included — orders of magnitude below what they observed. They note that the correlation distance the classical mechanism predicts played no role when they varied the gradient moments, and they conclude flatly: "It is now clear that we have not measured iZQC."

So the specific classical mechanism proposed against them has been answered. Three things still keep this at *mixed*. It is the authors' own defence, not an independent adjudication. Their classical bound is computed from expressions derived for chemical solutions, which they acknowledge. And nobody outside the original laboratory has implemented the pulse sequence. Note also what the result would and would not do if fully validated: it would establish non-classical function in a living brain, a landmark independent of Orch OR — and it would implicate no microtubule, since the known quantum systems in the measurement are the proton spins of bulk water.

## The argument that started it, and the machines now answering it

Penrose did not arrive at microtubules from biology. He arrived from Gödel. His argument, in the weaker form he retreated to under criticism, is that [human mathematical understanding is not the execution of any knowably sound formal algorithm]{claim=ORCH-C040} — and if mathematical insight is non-computable, something in the physics of the brain must be non-computable too, which is what sent him looking for new physics.

Critics say this has been overtaken by events, and the events are real. [An AI model has disproved a 1946 Erdős conjecture in discrete geometry, and DeepMind systems have reached Lean-verified silver and then officially graded gold medal standard at the International Mathematical Olympiad]{claim=ORCH-C041}. This case verifies the Erdős result not through a company announcement but through [Will Sawin's paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579), which states the result, names the mathematicians who checked it, and sharpens the bound. The olympiad results are firmer still: proofs machine-checked in Lean, methodology peer-reviewed, and the gold graded by IMO coordinators under contest conditions.

Here is where this case insists on a distinction both sides skip. **These results bear on the motivation for Orch OR, not on its mechanism.** Penrose's Gödel argument is why he went looking; it is not a premise of the claim that microtubules do the looking. Refute it completely and every microtubule and anesthesia claim above stands exactly where it was — the biology simply loses its original reason for having been proposed. Vindicate it completely and you still have no reason to think microtubules are the implementer rather than something else. That is why both claims in this theme are assessed as low-diagnosticity for the headline thesis, and it is the single most useful thing the ladder does here.

Within the theme the argument is live. The Penrose-side response is that performance is not understanding, and that the boundary worth arguing about lies between results *inside* a framework and the invention of the framework. That response gets unexpected support from inside the laboratory doing the work: a DeepMind researcher who co-authored AlphaProof argues in a position paper that these systems have mastered induction, are rapidly conquering deduction, and remain structurally incapable of the abductive jump required to formulate the premises they then reason from. Against that, the honest counter-objection is that an argument no possible achievement can touch has bought its safety with its content. And this evidence line carries its own error history: an earlier round of AI Erdős claims collapsed when the solutions turned out to be already in the literature, and one was withdrawn within hours when a 1977 resolution by Erdős himself surfaced.

> **The case editor's own view, labelled as such.** The essay behind this theme concedes the scoreboard against its own sympathies: of the concrete examples Penrose offered, the testable ones have mostly settled against him — most cleanly the pawn-fortress chess position released in 2017, which modern engines handle correctly — and the examples aging best are the least testable. Its argument is that the claim was never that any *particular* insight is permanently non-computable, but that the open-ended capacity to keep generating new frameworks is: "the escalator, not the steps." Each formalized insight becoming computable in hindsight is then predicted by the view rather than damaging to it. Whether that is depth or unfalsifiability is left to the reader; the essay declines to decide, which is why it is usable here.

## The live accounts, side by side

- **Orch OR.** Conscious moments are objective reductions of an orchestrated microtubule quantum state. Predicts: a coherence or entanglement witness in physiological microtubules lasting on the order of tens of milliseconds; anesthetic suppression of that witness scaling with clinical potency; collapse lifetimes scaling as ℏ/E_G in mesoscopic superpositions.
- **Interesting condensed matter, nothing more.** Microtubules are an ordered aromatic lattice with genuine collective photophysics and no neurally relevant coherence. Predicts: femtosecond-to-picosecond dephasing at 37 °C; optical effects perturbable by any small hydrophobic molecule, convulsants included; no potency correlation.
- **Multi-target classical pharmacology.** Predicts: target-level genetic dissection continues to explain agent by agent; tubulin effects behave like ordinary cell biology — transport, metabolism, integrity — rather than like a computation being switched off.
- **Radical-pair quantum biology, no microtubules required.** Predicts: the xenon isotope effect is magnetic-field dependent, and isotope and redox manipulations move microtubule density at matched chemistry.
- **Non-classical brain, non-cytoskeletal site.** Predicts: the zero-quantum-coherence signal replicates in other hands and survives phantom validation, while showing no dependence on microtubule integrity.
- **Collapse physics on its own track.** Predicts: the ℏ/E_G scaling shows up, or fails to, in levitated-nanoparticle or condensate experiments, with no biological commitment either way.

Each of these makes a different, cheap-to-state prediction, and the decisive comparisons are all unrun.

## The conventional account, taken seriously

The alternative is not a shrug. On anesthesia specifically it has causal evidence of a kind Orch OR does not: [a single engineered residue change in the GABA_A receptor β3 subunit abolishes the immobilizing action of etomidate and propofol and profoundly reduces their hypnotic effect]{claim=ORCH-C003}. Change one amino acid, lose the drug. Nothing remotely comparable exists for tubulin, and any serious treatment of this topic has to reckon with the asymmetry.

The boundary of that result is where proponents have a legitimate opening. The same mutation only slightly reduces the effects of the volatile anesthetics enflurane and halothane, and the authors' own conclusion is that volatile agents "act via a broader spectrum of molecular targets." The volatiles are the agents most Orch OR experiments use. In the same knock-in line, the endpoints come apart: immobility is abolished, the hypnosis surrogate is reduced but not abolished. And [the stronger claim that anesthesia and cognition are *fully* accounted for classically, with no quantum contribution]{claim=ORCH-C004} is assessed as unresolved rather than supported — largely on the conventional literature's own testimony, since Eger and colleagues report that two decades of focused investigation identified no ligand- or voltage-gated channel, and no combination of them, sufficient to mediate immobility from inhaled agents.

Which brings us to the proponents' best unanswered argument, and it is worth stating in their terms. Quantum-chemical modelling of anesthetic binding to delocalized electron sites in tubulin reportedly predicts the clinical potencies of several volatile agents — essentially reproducing the Meyer–Overton correlation, the oldest quantitative regularity in anesthesiology — and proponents assert that [no other candidate molecular target has a published model that does the same]{claim=ORCH-C057}. That claim is asserted in a commentary with no survey behind it, and the underlying computation is proponent-authored and untested prospectively. But nobody has produced the survey that would refute it either, and no rival target-level model reproducing Meyer–Overton has appeared. It is a real hole in the conventional account's coverage of the inhaled agents, and it points directly at an experiment nobody has run.

Where the conventional account is thinnest, though, is explanation rather than mechanism. It gives an increasingly detailed story of how consciousness is switched off and no principled account of why any of that activity is experienced, or why a conscious moment should have a characteristic duration. Orch OR at least attempts both. Attempting an explanation is not evidence for it.

## The crux, and what would change our mind

The disagreement does not live where the public argument puts it. Not in whether quantum mechanics operates inside proteins, and no longer in whether microtubules are electrically and optically interesting — measurements now say they are.

It lives in one unmeasured gap: between demonstrated collective electronic transport over roughly one tubulin dimer on femtosecond physics, and the long-lived, spatially extended coherent state the theory requires. Nobody has specified a density-matrix observable in physiological microtubules, measured its dephasing at 37 °C, and tested whether anesthetics suppress it in proportion to clinical potency. Until that number exists, "warm and wet kills it" and "warm quantum biology saves it" are two calculations arguing with each other.

Thirty years is a long time for a theory's central quantity to go unmeasured, and the theory bears some responsibility. Its published parameter values are consistent across two decades — 25 milliseconds, two times ten to the tenth tubulins, the same arithmetic throughout — but no acceptance criterion appears anywhere in the corpus: no required coherence time, no coherence length, no participating degrees of freedom, no threshold that would let a measurement count as pass or fail. The physical carrier itself changed in the 2014 revision, so results against the earlier conformational mechanism no longer bear on the current dipole one. Each new photophysics result gets absorbed rather than scored, and the clearest illustration is a proponent commentary that converts a fluorescence quantum-yield measurement into "definitive biophysical evidence that microtubules support quantum optical effects" in a single step, without the dephasing question being raised at all. That is a defect in specification, not evidence against content — but it is the defect that makes everything else harder to settle.

So, concretely:

- **A prespecified coherence or entanglement witness measured in physiological microtubules at 37 °C**, with the pass/fail threshold published in advance by proponents. A clean null near the theory's requirement would close the biological half. A positive result at tens of milliseconds would be a landmark in biophysics whatever anyone concludes about consciousness.
- **An anesthetic potency series against a metrologically stable microtubule observable**, including nonimmobilizers, picrotoxin and hydrophobic non-anesthetic controls, with free drug concentration measured. A Meyer–Overton slope for a microtubule observable would be hard to explain conventionally. Nonimmobilizers suppressing the signal just as well would close the anesthesia arm.
- **A tubulin anesthetic-pocket knock-in animal** that removes anesthetic binding while preserving polymerization and transport, with baseline receptor responses verified unchanged. This is the only design that could give the microtubule hypothesis causal evidence of the quality the receptor account already has.
- **A preregistered multicentre replication of the epothilone experiments**, with the direction of effect committed to in advance, acute and chronic regimens tested side by side, and brain drug concentration measured.
- **A mesoscopic test of the ℏ/E_G scaling**, on a track with no biology in it — plus the desk calculation that would say whether the one dynamics known to reproduce that rate exactly is already excluded by the radiation and acceleration-noise bounds.
- **A field-dependence test of the xenon isotope effect.** If the isotope ordering changes with ambient magnetic field, the anomaly belongs to spin chemistry and not to microtubules. If it does not, the field-fitted model is wrong and the anomaly returns to unexplained.

None of these requires believing the theory first. That is the most useful thing that can be said about a case this contested: every rung on it is separately testable, and almost none of the tests has been run.

assessment.synthesis:
Orch OR is a conjunction and must be graded as one: gravitational objective reduction has to be real (ORCH-C030), neuronal microtubules have to hold a suitable quantum state for roughly the duration of a conscious moment (ORCH-C010), and that reduction has to be the conscious moment (ORCH-C001). The observation rung is respectable — ORCH-E001 and ORCH-E004 are quantitative and partly independent, and ORCH-E056 now adds cross-laboratory support for the direction of the quantum-yield trend — but what they license is only that microtubules are electronically and radiatively nontrivial (ORCH-C013), which is ordinary condensed-matter behaviour in an ordered aromatic lattice and is the rung most often mistaken for vindication of the whole theory. The observable itself is not yet metrologically stable: ORCH-E075 puts the polymerization effect anywhere between +6% and +47% depending on scattering treatment, ORCH-E076 through ORCH-E079 show the sign reversing at the tryptophan-selective wavelength, and ORCH-E080 records that structural variability suppresses the cooperative enhancement the scale-bridging argument needs.

The mechanism rung is where the argument most likely fails. ORCH-E036 shows no unconditional proponent-side estimate reaching the theory's own 25 ms exemplar; ORCH-E035 shows the corpus fixing parameter values but no pass/fail threshold for any direct coherence test, so a future measurement could be absorbed either way; and ORCH-E072 and ORCH-E073 show the newest modelling reporting radiative, not dephasing, lifetimes in a bath with no solvent, ions or vibrations in it. ORCH-E081 through ORCH-E083 catch the absorption happening in one step.

The physics conjunct is now squeezed from three directions rather than one. ORCH-E017 and ORCH-E049 are two independent underground nulls in the radiation channel; ORCH-E046 bounds the regularization length above any nuclear size through mechanical acceleration noise, which the "Penrose predicts no radiation" escape (ORCH-E019) does not reach; and ORCH-E051 shows at least one dynamics reproducing Penrose's rate exactly with a fixed prefactor, so the escape is now a claim about which dynamics rather than about whether any dynamics lands on the relation. It survives as unresolved rather than contradicted only because ORCH-E071 and ORCH-E052 record, from the co-originator, that the rate carries an unspecified constant and that the dynamics is precisely what the two originators do not agree on.

On anesthesia, the flagship experiment's own convulsant comparison (ORCH-E003) shows the assay is not anesthesia-specific, and the best-designed independent animal study (ORCH-E013) has a stabilizer and a destabilizer shifting sensitivity in the same direction. The xenon line remains non-localizing and, after ORCH-E037 through ORCH-E040, thin: calculated headline values, dispersions of unstated type, a design that cannot support a two-covariate test, and eight years without replication, with ORCH-E038 defending only the shape of the pattern — and ORCH-E044 now supplying a quantum rival that sites the spin chemistry outside the cytoskeleton entirely.

Sensitivity: the record whose removal would most change the case is ORCH-E013, the only independent, blinded, full concentration–response animal study and the main reason ORCH-C012 is mixed rather than provisionally supported. Without it the anesthesia arm would look considerably cleaner. Even so the case verdict survives unchanged, because the verdict rests on an absence — no coherence time, dephasing time, or entanglement witness has ever been measured in a microtubule — and no single record can remove an absence. The record whose removal would most change the *reasoning* is ORCH-E036, which is what converts "unmeasured" into "unmeasured and, on the corpus's own published numbers, not yet reached on paper either."
assessment.steelman: The strongest argument this assessment does not answer is the Meyer–Overton argument, and it should be stated at full strength. The correlation between anesthetic potency and lipid solubility is the oldest quantitative regularity in anesthesiology and the one every mechanistic account has to earn. Quantum-chemical modelling of anesthetic binding to delocalized electron sites in tubulin reportedly predicts the clinical potencies of several volatile agents and essentially reproduces that correlation (ORCH-E010, restated at ORCH-E084 through ORCH-E086), and proponents assert that no other candidate molecular target — receptor, channel or membrane — has a published model that does the same (ORCH-C057). Set that beside ORCH-E031, in which senior figures in anesthetic mechanisms report that two decades of focused work identified no ligand- or voltage-gated channel, and no combination of them, sufficient to mediate immobility from inhaled agents, and beside ORCH-E015's own conclusion that volatile agents act through a broader spectrum of targets than the β3 receptor result covers. The proponent case is then not "microtubules are quantum" but something narrower and harder: for the inhaled agents — the agents most of this literature uses — the one structure that reproduces the field's founding quantitative regularity from first-principles binding chemistry is the structure Orch OR nominates, and the rival account concedes it has no sufficient target. This assessment discounts that argument because the modelling is computational and proponent-authored, because the uniqueness claim is asserted in a commentary with no survey behind it, and because ORCH-E003 shows the associated optical assay responding to a convulsant as well. But no survey refuting the uniqueness claim exists either, and no rival target-level model reproducing Meyer–Overton has been produced in the years since. The hole in the conventional account is real, and we cannot fill it.
assessment.whatIsClaimed: That each conscious moment is a Penrose objective reduction — a gravitationally induced collapse at time τ ≈ ℏ/E_G — of a quantum state orchestrated across tubulin proteins in neuronal microtubules, and that general anesthetics abolish consciousness substantially by disrupting that state rather than only by acting on receptors and circuits.
assessment.whereDisagreementLives: Not in whether quantum mechanics operates inside proteins (it does, trivially, in all chemistry), and no longer in whether microtubules are electrically and optically interesting (measurements now say they are). The disagreement lives in a specific unmeasured gap: between demonstrated collective electronic transport over roughly one tubulin dimer — about 6.6 nm, on femtosecond-to-picosecond physics — and the long-lived, spatially extended coherent or entangled state Orch OR requires, of order tens of milliseconds across many tubulins and neurons. No experiment has specified a density-matrix observable in physiological microtubules, measured its dephasing at 37 °C, and shown anesthetics suppressing it in proportion to clinical potency; and the theory's own corpus has never published the threshold that would let such a measurement count as pass or fail. A second, smaller disagreement lives one level down, in metrology: the leading optical observable is not yet stable enough to correlate against anything, since its effect size spans nearly an order of magnitude and its sign flips at the tryptophan-selective wavelength depending on how scattering is subtracted. On the physics side the disagreement has relocated from "has the model been excluded?" (the parameter-free stochastic version has, twice) to "does any dynamics that reproduces Penrose's rate survive the radiation and acceleration-noise bounds?" — a question that is now answerable at a desk.
assessment.whatWouldSettleIt: Five things, none of which requires believing the theory first. (1) A prespecified coherence or entanglement witness measured in physiological microtubules at 37 °C, with the required dephasing time, coherence length and participating degrees of freedom published by proponents in advance — without which any number can be absorbed either way. (2) Before that, closure of the scattering ambiguity in the microtubule quantum-yield observable, so that a single value and sign exist at 280 and 295 nm. (3) An anesthetic potency series against that observable spanning at least eight agents, including nonimmobilizers, picrotoxin and hydrophobic non-anesthetic controls, with free aqueous concentration measured and the predicted correlation registered in advance. (4) A tubulin anesthetic-pocket knock-in animal that abolishes anesthetic binding while preserving polymerization and transport, with baseline receptor function verified unchanged — the only design that could give the microtubule account causal evidence of the quality the β3 receptor result already has. (5) On a wholly separate track, a mesoscopic superposition test of whether collapse lifetime scales as ℏ/E_G, plus the desk calculation of whether the one construction known to reproduce that rate exactly is already excluded by the Gran Sasso, Majorana and LISA Pathfinder bounds. Positive results on the biology without the physics, or the physics without the biology, would each leave the conjunction unproven.
assessment.bestConventionalExplanation: Classical neural computation in a warm, wet, decohering brain: cognition implemented in membrane potentials, ion channels, synaptic weights and network dynamics, with consciousness an organizational property of that activity rather than a quantum-physical event. On the anesthesia side the conventional account is multi-target molecular pharmacology, and it has causal evidence Orch OR does not: a single point mutation in the GABA_A receptor β3 subunit (N265M) abolishes the immobilizing action of etomidate and propofol and profoundly reduces their hypnotic effect, while volatile agents act through a broader distributed set of channel and circuit targets. On this account the microtubule findings are ordinary cell biology and ordinary condensed-matter physics: an ordered aromatic lattice has collective photophysics whether or not anything computes with it, small hydrophobic molecules perturb that photophysics whether or not they are anesthetics (which is why a convulsant does it too), and microtubule-modulating drugs change anesthetic sensitivity through transport, metabolism and cellular integrity — which is the most natural reading of a stabilizer and a destabilizer shifting sensitivity in the same direction. The account requires no new physics and explains why anesthetic endpoints fractionate into hypnosis, amnesia, immobility and analgesia. Its two acknowledged gaps are that it offers no principled account of why any of this activity is experienced, and that for the inhaled agents it has not yet named a sufficient molecular target or reproduced the Meyer–Overton correlation from one.

components.label: Collective electronic and electromagnetic dynamics in microtubules
components.note: Quantitative, partly independent, and now cross-laboratory in direction — but the magnitude of the flagship optical effect is unstable to the scattering correction, and the effect is condensed-matter physics of an ordered aromatic lattice, not evidence of computation.

components.label: Physiological quantum coherence of the required duration and extent
components.note: The central quantity has never been measured. Two calculations disagree by seven to eight orders of magnitude; the proponents' own unconditional estimate falls two to three orders short of their own 25 ms exemplar; the newest modelling reports radiative, not dephasing, lifetimes.

components.label: Anesthesia by disruption of a microtubule quantum state
components.note: Real anesthetic effects on tubulin and on animal anesthetic latency, but the assay responds to a convulsant as well, the best independent animal study runs the other way, and no quantum variable has been measured in any of it.

components.label: Gravitational objective reduction as physics
components.note: The parameter-free stochastic version is excluded by two independent underground nulls, and a mechanical-noise bound now closes the channel the radiation escape avoided. The lifetime relation itself is untested, and its co-originator reports the constant unspecified and the dynamics unagreed.

components.label: Non-classical signals in the living brain
components.note: A striking consciousness-dependent MRI signal whose authors have now quantitatively rebutted the specific classical mechanism proposed against it, still unreplicated outside one laboratory — and implicating no microtubule even if correct.

components.label: The non-computability motivation
components.note: AI systems have produced verified novel research-level mathematics, and the Penrose-side reply about framework invention is defended from inside the labs doing the work. Either way this theme bears on why the theory was proposed, not on whether microtubules implement anything.

researchPriority.reason: The case turns on a single quantity that has never been measured, and the measurement is within reach of existing ultrafast-spectroscopy capability. Two of the highest-value items are desk work: publishing a 310 K dephasing prediction with a pass/fail threshold before the spectroscopy is run, and calculating whether the one dynamics that reproduces Penrose's rate exactly is already excluded by the bounded radiation and acceleration-noise channels. A third — closing the scattering ambiguity in the quantum-yield observable — is cheap and blocks every potency experiment downstream of it. Several of these would be worth doing for quantum biology, anesthetic mechanism and quantum foundations regardless of anyone's views about consciousness, and the contradiction between two laboratories on the epothilone result is an unresolved empirical fact that should not be left standing.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The thesis is a conjunction of an untested physical proposal (ORCH-C030) and an unmeasured biological one (ORCH-C010), and neither conjunct has been established or refuted. The supporting literature is a review by a scientist who is also senior author of its main behavioural evidence (ORCH-E028); the principal published critique is a three-page commentary whose argument this ledger has not read in full (ORCH-E016); and the modellers whose work is most often cited in its favour state explicitly that nothing in their results implies microtubules must use quantum correlations (ORCH-E055). ORCH-E035 records the decisive structural problem: the corpus fixes parameter values but no acceptance criterion, so no measurement can currently count as confirming or refuting it. That is unresolved in the strict sense — not a hedge, a description of the evidential state.

treatment.plainLanguage: The headline idea: a conscious moment is a quantum state inside neurons collapsing under gravity.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis; every other featured claim is graded partly by how much it moves this one.
treatment.strongestObjection: A theory that has gone thirty years without publishing a threshold at which a measurement would count against it is not yet in a position to be confirmed by measurements either, and its two required conjuncts are independently in trouble.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A coherence or entanglement witness measured in physiological microtubules at a duration and extent the theory names in advance
A mesoscopic demonstration that collapse lifetime scales as ℏ/E_G
A clean physiological null on the coherence witness, which would refute the conjunction whatever the physics does
Proponent publication of a pass/fail threshold, which would at least make the claim scorable

claimAssessments.reasoning: There are real anesthetic effects on microtubule photophysics (ORCH-E002) and on animal anesthetic latency (ORCH-E011, ORCH-E012), and β-tubulin is a genuine anesthetic binding target found by a laboratory with no stake in the theory (ORCH-E009). But nothing in this chain measures a quantum state. Three records hold the verdict down. ORCH-E003: in the flagship experiment a convulsant affected the same assay comparably, so the assay is not anesthesia-specific. ORCH-E013: the only independent, blinded, full concentration–response animal study found the opposite direction, with a destabilizer behaving like a stabilizer. ORCH-E015: the rival account has target-level causal evidence — one residue change abolishing a drug's action — that this account has nothing comparable to. ORCH-E014's xenon anomaly is quantum-specific but says nothing about location, and ORCH-E044 now offers a spin-chemistry route sited outside the cytoskeleton.

treatment.plainLanguage: That anesthetics put you under mainly by wrecking a quantum state in microtubules.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The most testable route into the thesis; a clean potency correlation here would be hard for the classical account to absorb.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every effect reported is compatible with anesthetics being small hydrophobic molecules that perturb a delicate optical observable and a busy cytoskeleton, and the one specificity control in the flagship experiment — a convulsant — behaved like the anesthetics.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A preregistered potency correlation across eight or more agents with nonimmobilizers and hydrophobic non-anesthetic controls behaving as the hypothesis requires
A tubulin anesthetic-pocket knock-in animal in which anesthetic resistance co-segregates with loss of the optical effect at unchanged receptor function
Nonimmobilizers suppressing the optical observable as strongly as anesthetics, which would close the line

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E015 is the strongest causal record in the case: a single engineered residue change in the GABA_A β3 subunit abolishes the immobilizing action of etomidate and propofol and profoundly reduces their hypnotic effect. The claim is drafted narrowly — multi-target pharmacology on network dynamics, with target-specific causal evidence for the intravenous agents — and that is what the evidence delivers. ORCH-E030 sharpens rather than undercuts it: within the same knock-in line, immobility and the hypnosis surrogate come apart, so the cleanest part of the effect is a spinal endpoint. The claim's own scope excludes the volatile agents, for which the same paper's authors report a broader spectrum of targets.

treatment.plainLanguage: Conventional pharmacology explains a lot of anesthesia, and for the intravenous drugs it can point to the exact molecule.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Sets the evidential bar the microtubule account has to clear, and the asymmetry is currently decisive for the anesthesia comparison.
treatment.strongestObjection: The cleanest result is about immobility, a spinal endpoint, from intravenous agents — while most Orch OR experiments use volatiles, for which the same authors concede a broader and less-resolved target set.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Failure to replicate the β3(N265M) dissociation, which has precedent in this literature (the TREK-1 case)
A demonstration that the residual hypnotic effect in the mutants is large and receptor-independent
Target-level genetic evidence for volatile agents that closes the gap the authors themselves left open

claimAssessments.reasoning: This is the exhaustive version of the classical account — no quantum contribution anywhere — and it is graded separately from ORCH-C003 for good reason. It is not supported by the evidence that supports the narrow claim, and three records stand against completeness: ORCH-E031, in which senior anesthetic-mechanism researchers report that no channel and no combination of channels is sufficient for immobility from inhaled agents; ORCH-E030, in which the endpoints of the best-characterized intravenous agent fractionate; and ORCH-E014, a quantum-specific isotope effect with no classical polarizability explanation on offer. ORCH-E033 is a weaker pointer at a dissociation between reported experience and metabolic signal, and the authors of that study draw no quantum conclusion from it. A universal negative of this kind is close to untestable directly; it is graded unresolved on the residue its own literature reports.

treatment.plainLanguage: The strong version of the standard view: no quantum weirdness is involved anywhere in anesthesia or thought.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If this were established the case would close; its unresolved status is what keeps the quantum options alive at all.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is an unrestricted negative, and the conventional literature's own reviews report an unexplained residue for exactly the agents this case argues about.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A sufficient classical target or target combination for inhaled-agent immobility
A classical explanation of the xenon nuclear-spin effect at matched polarizability
Conversely, a replicated magnetic-field dependence of any anesthetic potency, which would refute it outright

claimAssessments.reasoning: The lifetime relation itself has never been measured. What has been tested is a stochastic completion of it, twice and independently: ORCH-E017 at Gran Sasso and ORCH-E070/ORCH-E049 in the Majorana Demonstrator, both null, both excluding the natural parameter-free version. ORCH-E046 adds a second channel — LISA Pathfinder's acceleration noise bounds the regularization length above any nuclear size — which matters because the published escape (ORCH-E019, that Penrose's criterion predicts no radiation) does not reach mechanical momentum diffusion. ORCH-E051 narrows the escape further: a semiclassical construction reproduces the rate exactly and fixes its prefactor, so the question is now which dynamics rather than whether any. It survives as unresolved rather than contradicted only on ORCH-E071 and ORCH-E052, in which the co-originator states that the rate carries an unspecified constant, that its parameter-freedom may be illusory because it diverges for point masses, and that he and Penrose disagree about how the collapse happens at all.

treatment.plainLanguage: Penrose's physics: big enough quantum superpositions collapse on their own, on a clock set by gravity.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: One of the two conjuncts; if the collapse physics is wrong, no amount of microtubule biology saves the thesis.
treatment.strongestObjection: Escaping two independent radiation nulls and a mechanical-noise bound by being less specified than the model that was tested converts a refuted precise theory into an untested vague one — a worse position than it sounds.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A mesoscopic superposition experiment finding collapse lifetimes scaling as ℏ/E_G with decoherence independently characterized
A desk demonstration that the one construction reproducing the rate exactly is already excluded by the bounded channels, which would refute every proposed dynamics for it
A published dynamics that reproduces the rate while injecting neither energy nor momentum into matter

claimAssessments.reasoning: An interpretive claim about the nature of mathematical understanding rather than an empirical one, and the ledger contains no record that could settle it. The strongest pressure against it is the accumulation of formerly-human-only mathematical performance (ORCH-E022, ORCH-E023). The strongest pressure for it comes from inside the laboratories producing that performance: ORCH-E025, in which an AlphaProof co-author argues the systems have mastered induction, are conquering deduction, and remain structurally incapable of the abductive jump that formulates premises. ORCH-E026, the case editor's own audit, concedes that Penrose's testable examples have mostly settled against him and that the examples aging best are the least testable — which is the honest description of a claim retreating toward unfalsifiability.

treatment.plainLanguage: Penrose's original reason for looking: human mathematical insight is not any algorithm we could know to be sound.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Bears on why the theory was proposed, not on whether microtubules implement anything; refuting it leaves every biological claim exactly where it was.
treatment.strongestObjection: The formulation that survives the AI results — the open-ended capacity to invent frameworks, 'the escalator, not the steps' — is one no achievement could touch, which is a warning sign about content rather than a defence.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A formal result showing the Gödelian argument fails on its own terms
An AI system that demonstrably invents a new mathematical framework rather than working inside one
A proponent-endorsed statement of what achievement would count against the claim

claimAssessments.reasoning: This is the case's central absence. No coherence time, dephasing time, coherence length or entanglement witness has ever been measured in a microtubule under physiological conditions. In its place are calculations that disagree by seven to eight orders of magnitude — ORCH-E007 at 10⁻¹³ to 10⁻²⁰ s, ORCH-E008 replying at 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴ s after correcting the modelled state — and ORCH-E008 is filed as qualifying rather than supporting because even the proponents' own revised figure falls two to three orders short of their 25 ms exemplar. ORCH-E036 confirms this against the whole corpus: no unconditional proponent-side estimate meets the theory's own requirement, and the routes that reach physiological timescales are either explicitly conditional or inferred from unreplicated single-laboratory resonance measurements. ORCH-E072 and ORCH-E073 show the newest modelling reporting radiative lifetimes from a Markovian radiative-loss model with no thermal, solvent or ionic bath — not dephasing times. Unresolved here means unmeasured, not refuted.

treatment.plainLanguage: Whether microtubules in a living brain can actually hold a quantum state long enough and widely enough to matter.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The single most decisive rung in the case: a clean physiological null near the required timescale would close the biological half.
treatment.strongestObjection: Thirty years on, there is still no measurement and no published threshold at which a measurement would count as failure, so each new photophysics result gets absorbed rather than scored.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: 2D electronic spectroscopy or photon-echo measurement of a defined density-matrix observable in physiological microtubules at 37 °C, against denatured and disorder controls
A prepublished 310 K thermal-bath dephasing prediction for the same tryptophan geometry, with pass and fail values named
Any measured dephasing time at or near tens of milliseconds, which would be a landmark irrespective of consciousness

claimAssessments.reasoning: Two convergent lines support it. ORCH-E009 is causal and comes from an anesthesia laboratory with no theoretical stake: β-tubulin photolabelled by an anthracene anesthetic, binding localized near the colchicine site, polymerization inhibited, and stabilizers raising the immobilizing concentration in tadpoles. ORCH-E002 shows two clinical anesthetics reducing microtubule exciton diffusion. Against that, ORCH-E010 is computational rather than experimental, ORCH-E084 through ORCH-E086 are a commentary's restatement of that computation rather than new data, and the specificity problem at ORCH-E003 applies directly: a convulsant affected the same assay comparably. So anesthetics binding tubulin and altering microtubule optics is provisionally established; that the alteration has anything to do with unconsciousness is a separate claim and is not.

treatment.plainLanguage: Anesthetics do stick to tubulin and do change how microtubules handle light.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for the anesthesia arm but far from sufficient: ordinary pharmacology predicts binding and perturbation without any quantum content.
treatment.strongestObjection: Binding near the colchicine site and perturbing an optical observable is what small hydrophobic molecules do; a convulsant did it too, and neither observation distinguishes an anesthesia-specific mechanism.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A potency series in which suppression of the observable tracks clinical potency while nonimmobilizers and hydrophobic non-anesthetics do not
Direct binding measurements for clinical volatiles rather than a research anesthetic
Demonstration that the optical change is downstream of an unrelated effect such as polymer fraction or scattering

claimAssessments.reasoning: Two independent programmes report opposite directions and the contradiction is unresolved. On one side, ORCH-E011 (epothilone B delaying loss of righting reflex by 69 s in rats, d = 1.9, blinded, with a tolerance control) and ORCH-E012 (the same direction in mice, smaller, same laboratory and senior author, so not independent — a point ORCH-E029 records explicitly against the public claim of independent confirmation). On the other, ORCH-E013: randomized, blinded, four drugs, full concentration–response curves, finding chronic epothilone D making mice more sensitive and the destabilizer vinblastine moving sensitivity the same way. ORCH-E009 adds a third direction, with epothilone D producing resistance in tadpoles. ORCH-E032, the only human observation, measures a hemodynamic surrogate rather than a dose requirement. Manipulating microtubules does change anesthetic susceptibility; nothing coherent can yet be said about the direction or the operative variable.

treatment.plainLanguage: Drugs that stiffen or dissolve microtubules do change how easily animals go under — but nobody can say which way.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would be strongly diagnostic if the direction were consistent; as it stands the incoherence itself argues for a non-specific variable.
treatment.strongestObjection: A stabilizer and a destabilizer shifting sensitivity in the same direction is what general cellular disruption looks like, not what a stability-dependent quantum state looks like.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A preregistered multicentre replication testing epothilone B and D, acute and chronic, with the direction committed in advance and brain drug concentration measured
Evidence that the operative variable is polymer stability rather than transport, metabolism or redox state
A spin-chemistry test (isotope and field manipulation) explaining the same-direction anomaly mechanistically

claimAssessments.reasoning: Multiple partly independent lines converge. ORCH-E001 measures energy migration over about 6.6 nm, which the authors report is not sufficiently explained by accepted Förster models even after accounting for tryptophan–tyrosine interactions, with the structure-dependence expected of a real effect (polymerization matters, protofilament number does not). ORCH-E004 predicts and measures a quantum-yield enhancement from collective tryptophan states, from a group outside the Hameroff–Penrose lineage. ORCH-E074 adds cross-laboratory support for the direction in a different preparation, and ORCH-E006 records structure-dependent delayed luminescence. The verdict is well supported as stated — microtubules are not passive scaffolding — and deliberately no stronger, because ORCH-E005 (the resonance line) is unreplicated and classical, and the magnitude of the quantum-yield effect is unstable to the scattering correction.

treatment.plainLanguage: Microtubules are not inert girders: they move electronic excitation and emit light in ways a passive-scaffold model does not predict.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The rung most often mistaken for vindication of the whole theory; ordered aromatic lattices behave like this whether or not anything computes with them.
treatment.strongestObjection: Collective photophysics in a periodic array of aromatic residues is unremarkable condensed-matter physics and carries no implication about coherence times, entanglement or consciousness.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Failure to replicate the 6.6 nm diffusion length in independent hands
Demonstration that the quantum-yield trend is an artifact of scattering or polymer fraction rather than collective states
Conversely, an independent replication of the scale-free resonance work, which would make the rung considerably more interesting

claimAssessments.reasoning: The measurement is quantitative, published in a strong general chemistry venue from a mainstream ultrafast-spectroscopy laboratory, and internally structured in the way a real effect should be: ORCH-E001 reports the diffusion length depending on polymerization state but not protofilament number. ORCH-E002 records the anesthetic reduction. Two caveats keep it at well supported rather than established: no independent replication, and the theory's own authors are co-authors, so this is a collaboration including the proponents rather than an outside test. ORCH-E003 does not touch the measurement itself — only what it can be taken to mean.

treatment.plainLanguage: Electronic excitation travels about 6.6 nanometres through a microtubule — further than standard theory predicts — and anesthetics shorten the trip.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A genuine anomaly at the scale of a single tubulin dimer, many orders of magnitude short of what the thesis needs in time and space.
treatment.strongestObjection: 6.6 nm is roughly one dimer and the physics is femtoseconds to picoseconds; the reduction was measured at 50 μM without free aqueous concentration established, and a convulsant produced a comparable effect.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication in a laboratory with no proponent co-authors
An improved Förster-type treatment that accounts for the 6.6 nm figure conventionally
Measurement of free drug concentration showing the anesthetic effect occurs outside the clinical range

claimAssessments.reasoning: Downgraded from provisionally supported on the metrology records. Support: ORCH-E004 predicts and measures a quantum-yield enhancement with hierarchical organization, and ORCH-E056 reproduces the direction cross-laboratory in porcine tubulin at 280 nm with statistical significance on both absorbance branches. Against: ORCH-E075 shows the effect size at 280 nm ranging from about +6.1% to +46.8% purely on the choice of scattering treatment, and ORCH-E076 through ORCH-E079 show that at 295 nm — where excitation is most selective for tryptophan, and therefore where comparison with a tryptophan-only excitonic model is most meaningful — the two treatments reverse sign (about −58.6% against +12.7%), with the authors declining to assign any effect size. An observable whose sign is undetermined at the diagnostic wavelength cannot be said to increase in the direction a specific model predicts. ORCH-E080 adds that structural variability suppresses the cooperative enhancement the model's strong reading relies on.

treatment.plainLanguage: Building tubulin into microtubules seems to make them glow more efficiently — but how much, and at the most informative wavelength even whether, depends on how scattered light is subtracted.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The collective-optics observable that any anesthetic potency series would be run against; until it is metrologically stable, potency correlations against it cannot count.
treatment.strongestObjection: A steady-state quantum-yield increase has several conventional explanations, and this dataset cannot fix the sign of the effect at 295 nm, let alone attribute it to superradiance.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Re-measurement in cuvette and integrating-sphere geometries with independent turbidity measurement and measured polymer fraction, yielding a single value and a fixed sign at both wavelengths
A measured radiative-rate enhancement rather than a yield trend, which is what the collective model actually predicts
A scattering-controlled null or reversal at 280 nm

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E005 is the only record, graded weak, and its two problems compound rather than add. The measurement is an electromagnetic resonance structure — a classical observable, so self-similar frequency ratios across scales are not a coherence or entanglement witness and would not become one on replication. And no independent laboratory has reproduced it in over a decade, on bespoke apparatus spanning an unusually wide frequency range, in a low-profile venue; the same group's earlier electrical work is not independent corroboration. The case's own primer calls independent replication here the missing piece. Unresolved is the right grade: the claim is neither supported nor refuted, it is unexamined by anyone else.

treatment.plainLanguage: The same nested pattern of resonant frequencies reportedly shows up in a single protein, in a microtubule, and in part of a neuron.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If real, this is the scale-bridging mechanism the thesis needs to get from molecules to brains — which is exactly why an unreplicated version of it cannot be leaned on.
treatment.strongestObjection: Thirteen years without replication, on custom apparatus, measuring a classical quantity that no amount of confirmation would turn into evidence of coherence.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication outside the originating lineage, with published protocols, raw data and blinded analysis
Demonstration that the resonance structure is an instrumental artifact of the measurement bandwidth
Evidence linking the resonances causally to spike timing in living neurons in independent hands

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E011 is the cleanest behavioural record on the proponent side: blinded, large standardized effect (d = 1.9), with a control against anesthesia tolerance. ORCH-E012 reproduces the direction across species at 29 s and d = 0.8. Two things hold the verdict here rather than higher. The mouse study is the same laboratory and senior author, so it is a replication of direction within one programme, and its own abstract concedes the effect is not large against inter-animal variability; ORCH-E029 records that the public claim of independent confirmation does not hold. And the rat design is N = 8, male only, latency at a single high isoflurane concentration, and not counterbalanced. The observation stands as reported; what it means is a separate matter.

treatment.plainLanguage: Rats and mice given a microtubule-stabilizing drug take measurably longer to lose consciousness under isoflurane.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Real behavioural effect, but epothilone B changes stability, transport, metabolism and cellular integrity at once, so it does not discriminate between explanations.
treatment.strongestObjection: No quantum variable was measured, the two studies share a programme, and an independent laboratory using the fuller design found the opposite direction with a different epothilone.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication of the acute epothilone-B effect in counterbalanced crossover with both sexes and measured brain concentration
Evidence that the delay is explained by transport, metabolism or pharmacokinetics
A dose–response relationship rather than single-concentration latency

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E013 is the most methodologically complete animal study in the case: independent of the Wellesley programme, randomized, blinded, four drugs plus an opioid control, and full incremental concentration–response curves with published confidence intervals rather than latency at one concentration. The reported EC50 shifts are large and tightly bounded. The authors' own limitations are recorded — chronic dosing, an imperfect vehicle control for poorly soluble compounds, a righting-reflex rather than MAC endpoint, and epothilone D altering blood pH and CO₂ — which is why this is well supported rather than established. Its most informative feature is the one no stability-based account predicts: the destabilizer moved sensitivity the same direction as the stabilizer.

treatment.plainLanguage: An independent laboratory found chronic microtubule stabilization making mice more sensitive to anesthetic, not less — and a microtubule-destroying drug did the same thing.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The strongest single record against the anesthesia arm as usually stated, and the main reason the stabilizer literature cannot be read as a rule.
treatment.strongestObjection: Different compound and a two-week regimen rather than a single injection, so it constrains the generalization rather than refuting the acute effect directly; chronic modulation invites compensatory remodelling.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A head-to-head multicentre replication in which epothilone D acutely behaves like epothilone B
Evidence that the chronic effect is driven by the documented pH and CO₂ changes rather than by microtubules
A mechanistic account — spin-dependent redox chemistry is the live candidate — under which a stabilizer and a destabilizer should move sensitivity the same way

claimAssessments.reasoning: The observation stands on a single study (ORCH-E014): 80 randomized mice, four isotopes, identical calculated polarizability, a 40–50% potency gap across the spin boundary, in a flagship anesthesiology venue. ORCH-E038 defends the shape of the pattern descriptively — two mass units change potency by a few per cent within each spin pair while one mass unit across the boundary changes it by thirty, which a smooth mass confound cannot produce. But the weaknesses are severe and cumulative. ORCH-E040: the headline xenon-alone values are calculated from co-administration with isoflurane rather than directly measured, and the published dispersions are of unstated type. ORCH-E037: the dataset trips its own pre-set identification threshold, because the mass range is far too narrow for a linear mass term to be distinguished from a constant, so no two-covariate inferential test is possible either way. ORCH-E039: in eight years, no replication, no extension, no antecedent. ORCH-E042 restates the same four numbers rather than adding any.

treatment.plainLanguage: Xenon atoms that have nuclear spin are notably weaker anesthetics than chemically identical ones that do not.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Quantum-specific but entirely non-localizing: any spin-sensitive molecular target anywhere in the body produces it, and the published rival sites it at a receptor.
treatment.strongestObjection: One unreplicated four-arm experiment whose headline numbers are calculated rather than measured, whose error bars are of unknown type, and whose design cannot separate spin from mass inferentially.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Direct replication with stated dispersions, isotopic purity and a mass-matched isotope pair

A measurement under controlled external magnetic fields: a field dependence would relocate the anomaly to spin chemistry, and a null well above the model's stated range would falsify the published fit
Full-text access establishing whether the reported dispersions are standard deviations or standard errors

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held at mixed, with the reasoning updated because the published exchange is now complete. ORCH-E020 reports heartbeat-timed signals in living human brains that do not correlate with conventional MRI contrast and that change with conscious awareness.
