ORCH-E021 is a leading NMR methodologist's objection that the data provide no evidence for entanglement. ORCH-E087 through ORCH-E090 are the authors' quantitative reply: at their sequence parameters the classical intermolecular zero-quantum-coherence signal caps at 0.4% of initial magnetization and 0.13% with relaxation, orders of magnitude below what they observed; the ZQC correlation distance played no role when gradient moments were varied; and they conclude flatly that they have not measured iZQC. That answers the specific mechanism proposed against them. It does not settle the claim: the reply is the authors' own, its classical bound is computed from expressions derived for chemical solutions (as they acknowledge), no laboratory outside the original has implemented the protocol, and Warren's general point — that living tissue is complex, multicompartmental and imprecisely characterized by MRI — survives the rebuttal of one particular mechanism.

treatment.plainLanguage: An MRI protocol designed to see only non-classical signals picks up heartbeat-timed signals in awake human brains that fade as subjects fall asleep.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Potentially the most consequential result in the case for consciousness science generally, and almost non-diagnostic for Orch OR specifically: it implicates no microtubule, and the known quantum systems in the measurement are the proton spins of bulk water.
treatment.strongestObjection: Heterogeneous living tissue is precisely the regime in which classical multi-compartment effects can imitate exotic ones, and an entanglement witness must exclude them affirmatively rather than by elimination — in a protocol nobody else has run.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent implementation of the pulse sequence and analysis from the published description
Phantom validation against engineered ground-truth coupling before any consciousness correlation
Demonstration that the signal depends on microtubule integrity, which is the only step that would connect this line to the thesis at all

claimAssessments.reasoning: Upgraded from well supported on the arrival of an independent corroborating null. ORCH-E017 is the Gran Sasso search: a dedicated ultra-low-background germanium measurement, co-authored by the tested model's co-originator, finding no spontaneous radiation, tightening the bound on the effective nuclear mass-density size by about three orders of magnitude and ruling out, in the authors' own published words, the natural parameter-free version of the Diósi–Penrose model. ORCH-E047 and ORCH-E049 are the Majorana Demonstrator: no evidence of the 1/E signature between 19 and 100 keV across 37.5 kilogram-years of enriched germanium, a best-fit signal of 6.3 ± 398.8 counts, an almost order-of-magnitude improvement on the prior limit, and an explicit statement that this adds significance to the exclusion of the parameter-free model. Two independent collaborations in the same channel with consistent nulls and quantitative bounds puts the claim as stated beyond reasonable dispute.

treatment.plainLanguage: Two deep-underground detectors looked for the faint radiation that gravity-driven collapse should produce, found none, and ruled out the simplest version of the theory.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Directly damages the physics conjunct and is the highest-quality experimental record in the case; the escape from it is what keeps the thesis alive rather than any positive result.
treatment.strongestObjection: Both searches test a white-noise stochastic completion in the same radiation channel; the authors of the second note that coloured-noise extensions with a high-frequency cutoff evade X-ray bounds, and Penrose's own lifetime criterion makes no radiation prediction.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A detected excess consistent with the predicted 1/E spectral shape in a third underground dataset
A demonstration that the amplification or coherence assumptions mapping collapse to X-ray emission are wrong
Nothing short of that: the two nulls are independent and mutually consistent

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E022 is the load-bearing verification and is deliberately anchored on an independent mathematician's own paper rather than a company announcement: Sawin states that a team using an internal OpenAI model disproved the Erdős conjecture, names the mathematicians who checked it, and sharpens the bound himself. ORCH-E023 is firmer still on method — Lean-verified solutions to three of five non-geometry IMO problems including the hardest, peer-reviewed in Nature — and ORCH-E024 records officially graded gold standard in natural language under contest conditions. ORCH-E027 keeps the line honest: an earlier round of AI Erdős claims collapsed on inadequate literature search and one was withdrawn within hours, which is why the anchor is the arXiv paper rather than the announcement. The factual claim is well supported; ORCH-E025 contests what it means, not what happened.

treatment.plainLanguage: AI systems have produced correct new research mathematics, including disproving a 1946 conjecture, and have reached medal standard at the mathematical olympiad.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Bears on the motivation for Orch OR rather than its mechanism; refute or vindicate it and every microtubule and anesthesia claim stands where it was.
treatment.strongestObjection: Olympiad problems are solvable inside an existing framework by construction, and a DeepMind co-author of the system argues these models remain structurally incapable of the abductive jump that invents the framework — which is the boundary Penrose's defenders say was always the point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retraction or refutation of the unit-distance result
Evidence that the Erdős disproof reproduced an existing construction from the literature
An AI system inventing a new framework rather than working within one, which would move the interpretive claim as well as the factual one

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E044 is a modelling record, not a measurement: magnetic-field and hyperfine effects inserted into a two-rate kinetic model of tubulin polymerization, with recombination and relaxation rates chosen to reproduce a reported disorder of assembly under a hypomagnetic field — an experiment the authors themselves note reported no uncertainty. The group is the same one that produced the radical-pair model of xenon anesthesia, so this is not an independent line. What earns it a place in the case is not its current support but its structure: unlike the general-cellular-disruption reading of the same anomaly, it makes field- and isotope-dependent predictions that a modest experiment could falsify.

treatment.plainLanguage: A rival quantum mechanism: spin chemistry in a naturally occurring radical pair tunes how fast microtubules assemble, so their density depends on the ambient magnetic field.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A serious competing account — quantum biology without Orch OR — and the only one on the table that offers a mechanism for chemically opposite microtubule drugs shifting anesthetic sensitivity the same way.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is a parameter-fitted model reproducing a single uncertainty-free experimental ratio, from the same group that proposed the companion xenon model, with no anesthesia endpoint measured anywhere in it.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded comparison of microtubule density under nuclear-spin-bearing versus zero-spin zinc isotopes at matched chemical concentration
A field dependence of microtubule assembly that tracks the isotope effect, crossed with redox modulation
A null on both, which would leave general cellular disruption as the better reading of the stabilizer/destabilizer anomaly

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E046 derives the bound from LISA Pathfinder's published relative acceleration noise between two free-falling test masses, attributing the residual entirely to collapse-induced force noise and obtaining a Diósi–Penrose regularization length of at least 40.1 ± 0.5 fm — larger than any nucleus. The inference chain is short and the input measurement is a flight-qualified published figure. Two qualifications keep it at well supported rather than established: the bound is deliberately conservative, since Brownian thermal noise dominates and is not precisely known, and the calculation applies to the regularized model with a point-mass cutoff, which Penrose's own formulation treats differently. Its importance is the channel rather than the number: mechanical momentum diffusion is not photon emission, so the escape that saves Penrose OR from the radiation nulls does not reach here.

treatment.plainLanguage: A space mission measuring the tiniest residual jitter between two free-floating masses bounds the collapse model's short-distance cutoff above the size of any atomic nucleus.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Closes the second of two channels a gravity-related collapse could betray itself through, and it is the channel the 'Penrose predicts no radiation' defence does not cover.
treatment.strongestObjection: The bound attributes all residual acceleration noise to collapse, which is conservative by construction, and it constrains a regularized variant whose relationship to Penrose's own unregularized criterion is contested.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A demonstration that the mapping from collapse force noise to measured acceleration noise is invalid
A published collapse dynamics that reproduces the ℏ/E_Δ rate while injecting no momentum into matter
Revised LISA Pathfinder noise figures substantially larger than reported

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E047 reports the primary result directly: no evidence of the predicted 1/E X-ray signature between 19 and 100 keV across a 37.5 kilogram-year enriched-germanium exposure collected between 2015 and 2019, with a best-fit signal of 6.3 ± 398.8 counts. The experiment is an established underground collaboration and is independent of the Gran Sasso team, though it probes the same physical channel — so it corroborates the measurement rather than the mechanism. Its own stated limitation is that the constraint applies to white-noise formulations, with coloured-noise extensions at a high-frequency cutoff evading X-ray bounds, and that the Diósi–Penrose reading is a secondary re-expression of a search designed around continuous spontaneous localization.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second, independent deep-underground germanium experiment also found none of the radiation that spontaneous collapse should produce.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Removes the single-experiment dependency from the exclusion of the parameter-free collapse model without opening a new channel.
treatment.strongestObjection: Same radiation channel as the first null, so it tests the measurement rather than the mechanism, and the authors themselves note coloured-noise variants that evade it.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A signal excess matching the predicted spectral shape in this or a comparable dataset
A demonstration that the coherent-nuclear-emission assumptions inflate the sensitivity
Publication of a coloured-noise collapse model that is both viable and unconstrained by X-ray searches

claimAssessments.reasoning: This is the proponents' uniqueness claim, and it is unresolved in the strict sense: nobody has done the survey that would confirm or refute it. The only record is ORCH-E086, an assertion in a short proponent commentary, with ORCH-E084 and ORCH-E085 supplying the underlying attribution — that quantum-chemical modelling predicted the potencies of several volatile anesthetics from binding affinity at delocalized electron sites in tubulin, essentially reproducing the Meyer–Overton correlation. The primary behind that attribution is ORCH-E010, which is computational and proponent-authored and graded weak. No survey of receptor, channel or membrane models is cited, and none has been produced against it either. It is featured because it is the load-bearing premise of the case's strongest unanswered argument, and because ORCH-E031 makes the surrounding claim of a gap in the conventional account credible.

treatment.plainLanguage: Proponents claim no rival anesthetic target — no receptor, channel or membrane — has a published model that reproduces the classic potency-versus-solubility correlation, while tubulin does.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If true, it is the single strongest argument for a microtubule target in inhaled anesthesia; if the survey turns up a rival model, the proponents' best card disappears.
treatment.strongestObjection: An unsurveyed uniqueness claim in a commentary is not evidence, and the model it rests on is computational, proponent-authored, and has never been tested prospectively against an extended agent series including nonimmobilizers.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A systematic survey of published potency models for candidate anesthetic targets, either finding a rival that reproduces Meyer–Overton or confirming none exists
A prospective test of the tubulin model against an agent series including nonimmobilizers
Independent reimplementation of the tubulin quantum-chemical calculation

claimAssessments.reasoning: The finding comes from the modelling lineage that produced the superradiance argument in the first place, which makes it credible against interest: including molecular-dynamics-derived structural variability substantially reduces the maximal superradiant enhancement relative to an ordered reference lattice. ORCH-E080 records the accompanying fact that quantum yield nonetheless stays above 0.14 across the lengths examined, which is why the two things must be kept apart — a modest yield trend survives disorder, and the large cooperative radiative gain does not. It is provisionally rather than well supported because it is a single computational study, with disorder sampled from simulation rather than measured in a living cell.

treatment.plainLanguage: When realistic wobble and variation are put into the model of microtubule tryptophan networks, the dramatic cooperative light-emission enhancement largely disappears.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Targets the exact quantity the scale-bridging argument needs — cooperative enhancement — rather than the yield trend that is usually cited in its place.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is a simulation with simulation-derived disorder, not a measurement, and the authors still find quantum yields well above zero, so the collective picture is degraded rather than eliminated.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A measured radiative-rate enhancement in real microtubules at physiological temperature consistent with the ordered-lattice prediction
An independent disorder model in which the enhancement survives
Experimental determination of the actual structural variability in living microtubules
